title: Count the Number of Special Characters I
summary: Given a string, count how many letters appear in both lowercase and uppercase forms.
statement: Given a string, count how many letters appear in both lowercase and uppercase forms.
constraints: A letter is special when both its lowercase and uppercase forms occur somewhere in word.
Order and multiplicity do not matter.
Return the number of distinct special letters.
hints: A set removes multiplicity while retaining presence.
Iterate each lowercase alphabet letter once.
Count it only if both that character and its uppercase form belong to the set.
This visits every possible letter identity once and applies exactly the two-presence condition.
editorial: This visits every possible letter identity once and applies exactly the two-presence condition.

tests.explanation: Letters a, b, and c appear in both cases, so the result is three.
No uppercase form appears, so the result is zero.
